item.title: Brushstrokes bring Red Army martyrs' portraits for families
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
This photo shows the studio of a volunteer team focusing on painting portraits of martyrs, at the Academy of Fine Arts of Anhui Normal University in Wuhu, east China's Anhui Province, Sept. 25, 2026. During this year's Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, a volunteer team from the Academy of Fine Arts of Anhui Normal University was busy in Jinzhai County of Lu'an City in east China's Anhui Province, drawing portraits of Red Army martyrs who participated in the Long March, the historic military maneuver in modern Chinese history, and presented them to the families of the martyrs. Since November 2021, the Academy of Fine Arts of Anhui Normal University has formed a team to carry out a series of volunteer services focused on drawing portraits of martyrs. Up to now, hundreds of students have participated in these activities, jointly drawing more than 600 portraits of martyrs, which have become an important way for their families to express feelings of longing. Across time and space, the youthful faces of those who had fallen on the battlefield were finally seen again by their families back home. Tucked in the Dabie Mountains, Jinzhai county contributed tens of thousands of people to the Communist Party of China (CPC)-led revolution in the first half of the 20th century. A total of 12 main units of the Red Army originated from here. Now, the Anhui Normal University project to paint portraits of Red Army martyrs is giving some families a long-awaited face to go with the stories passed down for generations. Usually the volunteer team would first contact the relatives of martyrs and then study photographs of the martyrs' descendants to determine basic facial contours. They would then revise the portraits repeatedly, drawing on family descriptions of the martyrs' eyes, expressions and habitual looks, until these relatives feel the likeness is right. For teachers and students of the team, painting portraits of martyrs is not merely a simple sketch creation but also an immersive study tour of revolutionary history. The brows and eyes rendered by the artists' brushes have captured the youthful appearance of the martyrs and also provided a place for the remembrance to rest. The past events recounted by the relatives of the martyrs are a testament to the enduring revolutionary legacy of the Dabie Mountains from generation to generation. item.title: Shanghai wins 1st WIPO City of Innovation award
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
WIPO Director General Daren Tang (L) presents an award to Chinese city Shanghai during the Inaugural Award Ceremony for the first WIPO City of Innovation award at the headquarters of the WIPO in Geneva, Switzerland, Oct. 12, 2026. Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award. (Xinhua/Lian Yi) GENEVA, Oct. 12 (Xinhua) -- Chinese city Shanghai, Britain's Liverpool and Belgium's Charleroi were announced Monday by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) as winners of the first WIPO City of Innovation award. Launched for the first time in 2026, the WIPO City of Innovation award is open to cities across all 194 WIPO member states and is bestowed on visionary cities for their bold pledges to foster innovation and creativity over the coming year. The three winners were chosen from 15 finalist cities. According to WIPO, Shanghai's vision is to strengthen its position as an international hub for science, technology and intellectual property (IP), while fostering a broader culture of innovation and creativity. Its pledges include expanding IP education and services, opening innovation infrastructure and data, supporting cultural and creative industries, and strengthening connections between research, industry, entrepreneurs and investors. Zhou Yaming, Deputy Secretary-General of the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, said the award represents WIPO's strong recognition of Shanghai's innovative developments and its efforts in building a thriving IP ecosystem. "It also reflects the international community's endorsement of China's commitment to open innovation, mutual benefits and shared success," He said. Winners were selected by an independent international jury of high-profile experts in the cultural and creative sectors, urban planning, community development, and innovation-driven growth. Andrea Dempster Chung, member of the International Jury Panel and Co-Founder & Executive Director for Kingston Creative, said Shanghai's application was extremely impressive, not just because of its strong research and development base that the city already had, but for the sheer scale of its ambitions and the strength of pledges. "This would be pivotal in shifting the city's future and this is one of the reasons why Shanghai was selected," she said. ■ People attend the Inaugural Award Ceremony for the first WIPO City of Innovation award at the headquarters of the WIPO in Geneva, Switzerland, Oct. 12, 2026. (Xinhua/Lian Yi)

item.title: The warplanes fell, the memory endured
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
More than 80 years ago during World War II, ordinary Chinese villagers in east China's Zhejiang Province risked their lives to shelter and rescue downed American airmen. Decades later, traces of those wartime encounters still linger. What began in the midst of war has endured across generations, leaving behind a lasting legacy of friendship between the people of China and the United States.

item.title: China approves Visa subsidiary application to establish bank card clearing institution
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- China's central bank has approved an application from a subsidiary of Visa to set up a bank card clearing institution in China, a step forward in the country's financial opening up. Visa Information Technology (Beijing) Co. Ltd. is required to complete its preparations and apply to commence operations within a year, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) said on Tuesday. The bank card clearing business license will be issued after the PBOC and the National Financial Regulatory Administration jointly approve the application. "The approval of our Application to Prepare marks a significant step forward in Visa's long-standing commitment to China," said Ryan McInerney, CEO of Visa. "For more than 40 years, Visa has been an active contributor to China's dynamic payments landscape." "China is one of the world's most advanced and dynamic digital payments markets, supported by a highly innovative ecosystem and continued commitment to further financial sector liberalization," said Visa in a statement after the approval on Tuesday. Under current regulations, once it is approved to commence operations, Visa will be able to provide clearing services and issue bank cards denominated in renminbi (RMB). The company is currently permitted to provide such services in China only in foreign currencies. PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng met with Visa CEO McInerney on May 15 this year. They exchanged views on issues including China-U.S. economic and trade relations, and Visa's development in China. American Express secured approval in 2018 to establish a bank card clearing institution through its Chinese joint venture, Express (Hangzhou) Technology Service Co., which launched operations in 2020, becoming China's first foreign-funded bank card clearing institution. Mastercard likewise secured approval in 2020 and started operations in 2024. ■

item.title: U.S. should cease sending wrong signals to "Taiwan independence" separatist forces: Chinese foreign ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- The U.S. side should stop sending wrong signals to "Taiwan independence" separatist forces, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said at a regular media briefing on Tuesday. The one-China principle is a basic norm governing international relations and a prevailing consensus of the international community as well as the political foundation of China-U.S. relations, Mao noted. "The U.S. side should abide by the one-China principle and the provisions of the three China-U.S. joint communiques, handle the Taiwan question carefully, and stop sending wrong signals to 'Taiwan independence' separatist forces," the spokesperson said. ■

item.title: Xi calls for decisive progress in Healthy China advancement
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a national meeting on health in Beijing, capital of China. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Oct. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for efforts to firmly follow a path with Chinese characteristics in developing the country's health programs, to secure decisive progress in the Healthy China Initiative over the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030). Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a national meeting on health held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Xi stressed that people's health is a key benchmark of a nation's prosperity and strength. Since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, the Party has made a major decision to launch the Healthy China Initiative, promoting the establishment of the world's largest systems of medical services, traditional medicine, disease prevention and control, and healthcare security, said Xi, noting that the country has achieved historic accomplishments and made all-round progress in healthcare. He said the goal is to build a Healthy China, where health services are ensured in a balanced, inclusive, high-quality and efficient manner. Xi stressed that people's health should be factored into all policies and reflected in every aspect of work. Prevention, he said, is the most cost-effective and efficient approach to protecting public health. He called for greater emphasis on foundational health work, addressing risks at their source, and encouraging the public to adopt a sound understanding of health and take an active role in managing their own well-being. He also called for a stronger disease prevention and control system to guard against large-scale outbreaks. Xi underscored the need to optimize the functions and structural layout of medical institutions so that people can access medical care close to home and receive effective treatment. He also urged efforts to improve mechanisms for the preservation and innovative development of traditional Chinese medicine, strengthen basic research and original innovation in the health sector, and enhance the patient experience. Xi stressed that coordinating the development and regulation of medical services, medical insurance, and pharmaceuticals should be a key priority in reforming China's medical and healthcare systems. He also called for efforts to train and develop a sufficient number of highly qualified medical professionals. Efforts will also be made to actively promote the building of a global community of health for all, work with other countries to address major challenges in the health sector, and continuously improve the health and well-being of people around the world, he said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, delivers an important speech during a national meeting on health in Beijing, capital of China. The meeting was held in Beijing on Monday and Tuesday. Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi attended the meeting. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei)
